questions.q: What must be true for the role hierarchy to automatically widen access to an object, per this lesson?
options: The object's OWD must have Grant Access Using Hierarchies enabled
The object must be a custom object
The user must also have View All on the object
The role hierarchy must exactly match the company's org chart
questions.explain: The role hierarchy only widens access to an object when that object's OWD has Grant Access Using Hierarchies turned on.

questions.q: In which direction does access flow through the role hierarchy?
options: Downward only -- managers' records open up to their reports
Both directions equally between any two connected roles
Upward only -- those above a role in the chain gain access to records below
Sideways only, between peer roles in parallel branches
questions.explain: The lesson states the hierarchy flows strictly upward: managers see reports' records, never the reverse.

questions.q: Two users are peers reporting to the same manager, in separate branches. Does the role hierarchy give either one access to the other's records?
options: Yes, peers always share full access to each other's records
No -- parallel branches don't share access through the hierarchy alone
Only if their manager explicitly enables it per user
Yes, but only to records created in the same quarter
questions.explain: The lesson states peers in parallel branches see nothing extra from each other through the hierarchy.

questions.q: What does a role's detail page show beyond its position in the tree, per this lesson?
options: Nothing -- the position in the tree is the only information a role holds
Explicit Opportunity Access and Case Access language describing exactly what the role grants
The role's assigned permission sets
The field-level security for every object
questions.explain: Role detail pages include specific, readable Opportunity Access and Case Access settings, not just hierarchy position.

questions.q: Per this lesson, does the role hierarchy have to match the company's org chart?
options: Yes, Salesforce enforces that they be identical
No -- the role hierarchy exists purely to control data visibility and can be modeled differently, such as around sales territories
Yes, but only in orgs using Sales Cloud
No, and in fact they can never share any structure at all
questions.explain: The lesson explains the role hierarchy is often modeled on the org chart but isn't required to match it -- it exists for data visibility, not HR structure.
